headlines.text: That Saturday in 2023, a new champion was crowned for the AEW TBS Title as Julia Hart vs. Kris Statlander vs. Skye Blue battled it out, appearing on Full Gear, rated 7.07 ? a solid showing ? ending the champion's reign at 13 defenses. This stood as the 30th match in AEW TBS Title history ? a real landmark for that championship. Statlander hit her Saturday Night Fever on Skye Blue in the closing seconds, only for Julia Hart to shove her aside and steal the pin, becoming the youngest champion in AEW history at 22.

Rewind to 2022, when Chris Jericho vs. Bryan Danielson vs. Claudio Castagnoli vs. Sammy Guevara fought tooth and nail for the ROH World Heavyweight Title, appearing on Full Gear, rated 8.39 ? a hard-hitting, high-quality battle. Jericho survived a four-way with two Blackpool Combat Club members and his own stablemate Sammy Guevara, landing the Judas Effect on Castagnoli to retain the ROH World Title.

secondaries.text: 2023 brought us this moment: the AEW Women's World Title had a new owner by the end of the night as Toni Storm vs. Hikaru Shida battled it out, appearing on Full Gear, rated 4.79 ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. This stood as the 50th match in AEW Women's World Title history ? a real piece of championship history. Storm dethroned Shida with the help of her ally Luther and a metal-plate-assisted hip attack to become a three-time AEW Women's World Champion.

On a Friday in 2022, back when the AEW World Heavyweight Title changed hands as MJF vs. Jon Moxley battled it out, appearing on Full Gear, rated 7.78 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. In a title match built on a promise of fair competition, MJF revealed his collusion with William Regal, using a pair of brass knuckles to finally beat Moxley and become AEW World Champion.

It was 2022 when it was title-change night for the AEW Women's World Title as Jamie Hayter vs. Toni Storm battled it out, appearing on Full Gear, rated 7.82 ? a good, competitive contest ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. Hayter dethroned Toni Storm with a ripcord lariat to win the interim AEW Women's World Championship, a hard-hitting result that set up her run as a dominant new champion.
